name: Pobassoo's trepang fleet
traveler: Pobassoo and the Makassan trepang fleet
summary: For nearly two centuries, from about 1720 until Australia banned it in 1907, fleets of praus sailed from Makassar each December on the north-west monsoon to the coast of Arnhem Land, which they called Marege', to gather and boil trepang for the China trade, and came home on the south-east trades in April. In February 1803 Matthew Flinders met part of one fleet: its commander Pobassoo told him he led some sixty praus and a thousand men and had made the voyage six or seven times.

stops.note: The fleet sails south-east on the north-west monsoon.
The praus spread out along the coast, boiling and drying trepang in camps ashore.
Flinders finds six praus here and talks with Pobassoo.
Home on the south-east trades with the season's catch.
